title: the harness lives: the text of the harness is always text, the journal never refuses a record, a run without a summary degrades, and the record of a failure is bounded
intent: The live test of Yeah against a real provider found four defects that no offline check had seen, because every offline check had been written by the same hand as the code and had read the tools of the harness the way the code wrote them.  A `bash' tool whose output ends in a byte that is not valid UTF-8 killed the whole Emacs process: the refusal of JSON arrived inside the sentinel of the process, where no handler of the turn stands, and the run left no record of itself (exit code 255).  The same bytes took the record of the tool out of the journal, because the journal could not write them.  A compaction whose summary the provider did not write killed the run instead of degrading it, although the summary is an economy and not a necessity.  And the record of a failure held the whole conversation of the run: the refusal of a provider carries the conversation in it, and one record of the journal must be a record and not a transcript (the record of the failure of the second live run was 2.8 MB).  The wave repairs all four.  The text of the harness is decided in one place (`lib/yeah-text.el'): a byte that is not text becomes the replacement character, in both shapes it arrives in — a unibyte string of bytes and a multibyte string that holds a raw byte where the decoder refused one.  The journal never refuses a record: a record that JSON cannot write is written as a stand-in that says so.  The scheduler and the turn do not let an error of the harness escape into the sentinel of a process.  A run whose summary does not arrive prunes the old outputs of its tools, says so in the journal and goes on; a second failure without a summary ends the run with that reason.  The reason of a failure that goes into the journal is bounded at two thousand characters and names the cause.  The wave is numbered 45 and not 41: the waves 41 to 44 are the plan the owner named on 2026-11-16 (docs/PLAN.md 18), and that plan is not rewritten here.  The wave was executed before them because the four waves of the plan need a harness that lives to carry them.
objection: The wave changes what the harness writes into its journal, and a reader of an old journal and a reader of a new one see different records: the broken byte of a tool is now the replacement character and not the byte, and the reason of a failure is cut at two thousand characters and not whole.  The cut loses the tail of a reason, and a tail can hold the cause: the wave keeps the head of the reason and the fields that name the failure, and it says where the text was cut, but a reader who needs the whole refusal of the provider must go to the provider again.  The stand-in of the journal loses the payload of a record that JSON cannot write, and the record of a run is then incomplete: the journal says that it could not write the record and names the kind of it, but the work of the tool is not in the journal.  The wave does not repair the defect of the working directory of a session (`cwd' is still not applied to the tools, docs/PLAN.md 17.1), and it does not repair the shape of the provider that answers a plan instead of an action (the pilot of the harness, docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md).  The wave does not touch the plan of the owner: the waves 41 to 44 keep their numbers and their order.
refuted_by: the output of a tool or the text of the model is a string that JSON refuses; the journal raises an error on a record it cannot write, or stops taking the records that follow; the process of the harness dies with the bytes of a tool, or the journal holds no record of the tool; a run ends in the state 'failed' because the model wrote no summary; the record of a failure holds more than four thousand characters, or does not name the cause
note: All five controls were run against the code of this wave and bit; each of them made its check fail by an assertion of the check and not by a crash of Emacs.  The control of `the-text-of-the-harness-is-always-text' removes the reading of the output of a tool, and the check fails on the assertion `the output of the tool is not text that the journal can write'.  The control of `the-journal-never-refuses-a-record' makes the journal raise instead of writing a stand-in, and the check fails on the assertion `the journal refused to write a record: (user-error "the journal cannot write this record")'.  The control of `a-tool-that-returns-bytes-does-not-kill-the-harness' removes both readings of the broken bytes, and the check fails: the child process dies with the exit code 255 and the journal holds no record of the tool — the live defect, reproduced offline and end to end.  As it was registered in `spec.json', the control of the claim removed only the first of the two readings: the second part of the expression did not match the code, which had wrapped the call in `yeah-session--json-value', so the check passed under the control and the claim came out inconclusive.  It was repaired on 2026-11-19, and the claim was re-verified that day: `pass' and `negative control proven' (docs/PLAN.md section 16.61).  The control of `a-run-degrades-when-the-summary-does-not-arrive' makes the first failure of the summary end the run, and the check fails on the assertion that the run died.  The control of `the-record-of-a-failure-is-bounded' removes the cut, and the check fails: the record of the failure holds 200031 characters and the journal grew to 400503 bytes over two failures.  The wave found a defect of its own code before the checks caught it: the first version of `yeah-text-valid' returned a multibyte string as it was, and a multibyte string may hold a raw byte — the byte that the decoder of a process refused stays inside the string as a character whose code is at or above #x3FFF00, and JSON refuses that string as well.  The live crash of the harness was of that shape, and the fix of the first version did not cover it: the journal survived, but the record of the tool was replaced by a stand-in.  The module reads that shape now, and the check of the live path proves it: the journal holds the record of the tool with the replacement character in place of the broken byte.  The wave also repaired the checks of the repository that expected the old shape of the failure of a compaction, and it did not change the verdict of the claim of the supervision of a run.  The repaired harness was then run against a real provider with a real coding task (a console calculator, its tests, and the run of the tests): the model wrote the calculator (5 553 bytes) and its own tests (4 699 bytes, fifteen where the task asked for eight), the tests passed outside the harness with the code 0, and the run ended in the state `completed' after three nudges of the harness, because the provider answered with a plan where an action was asked for.  That run is also the first live proof of the repair: one command of the model (`head -c 3000' of the journal) cut a multibyte character in half, and the journal of the run is valid UTF-8 from the first byte to the last.  Two things the run did not do are written down and not hidden: the model never called the tool `finish' although the task asked for it, and its last message announced a verification that never happened, which the regexp of the plan does not read as a plan (docs/PLAN.md 17.1, docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md).
